title: MZ How hard is it to make a basic plugin command?

posts.author: chris-cote
posts.body:
Hi folks,
I have a lot of script calls I use in various common events which pass game variables into them which are set before running that common event, such as:
JavaScript:
$gameVariables.setSelfValue([$gameVariables.value(1), $gameVariables.value(2), $gameVariables.value(3)], $gameVariables.value(4));
(Variables 1-4 are set in the event, then this script is run as a common event)
So, I was wondering how hard it would be for someone with no JS knowledge to make a plugin that does nothing but add a plugin command which accomplishes the same thing, but takes parameters for each of those variables instead of referencing a game variable.
Something like:
A plugin command with these params:
Param1 = Number
Param2 = Number
Param3 = Number
Param4 = Number
Then the command runs:
JavaScript:
$gameVariables.setSelfValue([param1, param2, param3], param4);
The reason I want to do this is because I use plugin-specific script calls for things that I might need to change later. To keep things flexible, I'll put the script call in a common event, make it accept variables as it's values, and then set those variables outside the common event before running it. This way, if I need to replace that plugin or change the script call, I can change it in the common event without having to change every instance of that script call, as the values for every different case were set outside of it.
Using a plugin command cleans that up, and allows me to edit the plugin itself instead of a common event if I need to change the script call, and the use of the script call in events will look cleaner since it would be one plugin command instead of setting several variables and then running a common event.
Thanks!
For some context, the setSelfValue script in the example is from a self-variables plugin I use. It has its own commands already, and this is just an example.

Echowake
posts.body:
/*:
* @target MZ
* @plugindesc Adds a plugin command to call $gameVariables.setSelfValue with twelve numeric parameters.
*
@Author
Echowake
*
* @command SetSelfValue12
* @text Set Self Value (12 Params)
*
@desc
Calls $gameVariables.setSelfValue with eleven array values and one target value.
*
* @arg Param1
* @type number
* @text Value 1
*
* @arg Param2
* @type number
* @text Value 2
*
* @arg Param3
* @type number
* @text Value 3
*
* @arg Param4
* @type number
* @text Value 4
*
* @arg Param5
* @type number
* @text Value 5
*
* @arg Param6
* @type number
* @text Value 6
*
* @arg Param7
* @type number
* @text Value 7
*
* @arg Param8
* @type number
* @text Value 8
*
* @arg Param9
* @type number
* @text Value 9
*
* @arg Param10
* @type number
* @text Value 10
*
* @arg Param11
* @type number
* @text Value 11
*
* @arg Param12
* @type number
* @text Target Value
*
@desc
The value to pass as the second argument.
*/
(() => {
PluginManager.registerCommand("YourPluginName", "SetSelfValue12", args => {
const values = [];
for (let i = 1; i <= 11; i++) {
values.push(Number(args[`Param${i}`]));
}
const target = Number(args.Param12);
// Call your existing function
$gameVariables.setSelfValue(values, target);
});
})();
Here you go..i dont know what you variable or functions are but i expanded it to 12 so you not set on four. Hope this helps.

Solar_Flare said:
Making a plugin command in MZ isn't that difficult. The actual functional code would look something like this:
JavaScript:
const me = 'YourPluginName';
PluginManager.registerCommand(me, 'CommandName', function(args) {
    $gameVariables.setSelfValue([args.mapId, args.eventId, args.selfSwitch], args.value);
});
Then you'd need all the comment syntax to tell the editor how to handle your new command. That syntax would need to define what mapID, eventId, selfSwitch, and value actually mean in the above code.

One quick question for you - if I wanted to run a script call in a plugin like this, and wanted to use this.eventId() as a value in the script it runs when the plugin command is run from inside an event, is there a way to do that? (such as getting the ID of the event running the command)
I tried to add a command to my plugin for running this script call:
JavaScript:
Ritter.unspawnEvent(this.eventId(), true);
But, when running the command from the plugin, it doesn't seem to be working the way running the script in an event would work (to get its own ID) and crashes the game. I'm assuming the "this" is pointing to the plugin instead of the event running the command or something.
This is what I have for this script call:
JavaScript:
/*:
 * @target MZ
 * @plugindesc Adds commands to spawn and erase events.
 * @Author Chris Cote
 *
 * @command EventEraseSelf
 * @desc Erase the event running the command, and remove saved data for that event.
 *
*/
(() => {
PluginManager.registerCommand('SpawnEventCommands', 'EventEraseSelf', (args) => {
    Ritter.unspawnEvent(this.eventId(), true);
});
})();
